top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a distinct, independently reproduced principle (magic-wavelength trapping of many atoms) that is mature at the 1e-18 level and is already yielding clues from nature such as millimetre-scale gravitational redshift and bounds on drifting constants. Katori's proposal and first demonstration and Ye's drive to world-class accuracy make the two-name allocation clean and the citation scope exact; the metrology-precedent overlap with 2005 and 2012 is real but answered by citing the lattice invention precisely. Awarding is better than no prize.
